# Agent-orchestration control plane: 29 one-line faults, no test suite

This software keeps fleets of automated workers alive on a cluster: people watch them and talk to them from a terminal view and from group threads, drive the whole thing over an HTTP interface, and the workers in turn lean on hosted language services and on helper processes of their own. Complaints have been piling up from several directions at once and they do not line up with any single change anyone remembers making. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything users have managed to reproduce first-hand.

Start with people simply watching and talking. The exchange history shown in the terminal view for one worker goes wrong in two separate ways. The most recent job, when it belongs to that worker, is missing from the transcript altogether. And jobs are drawn under the wrong outcome: a job that ended in failure is drawn as still pending instead of showing its error text, while skipped jobs and jobs still under way come out as errors with no text, so a skipped job no longer shows its skip reason, nor the stand-in reason when none was recorded. Successful jobs still show their answers, and jobs belonging to a different worker are still kept out.
